extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, potential reviewers, SROs and academic researchers involved in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria, concerns, and informal standards for selecting and composing NIH (and similar) study sections and for choosing reviewers; includes debate about career-stage inclusion, diversity, expertise matching, reviewer quality, and virtual review innovations. Focused on practical selection and panel-composition issues rather than formal scoring of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow assistant professors to serve
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant Professors should not be excluded from serving on study sections; removing them (as urged by Toni Scarpa historically) is misguided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's main objection: assistant professors provide valuable perspective and should be included. Several commenters note assistant professors have served on panels and that excluding them reduces the pool of capable reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require prior NIH funding for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer pool should not be limited only to people who have already won NIH funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique that limiting to previously funded Professorial-rank people is ridiculous and excludes worthy reviewers (including some senior postdocs and newer faculty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include senior postdocs and non-faculty reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: More senior postdoctoral researchers and other non-faculty investigators who have relevant expertise should be eligible to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument that some senior postdocs are unfairly barred despite having appropriate expertise; expanding pool could diversify perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnic/racial/gender/geographic representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels should seek representation across race/ethnicity, gender, and geographic region as per official mandates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes SROs generally do a good job achieving these mandates. Commenters raise tradeoffs: underrepresented reviewers can become overburdened with service, which can harm their research productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional-type diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Study sections should include members from a variety of institution types (small teaching-focused colleges, R1 research universities, research institutes, public/private universities, medical schools, different departments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author reports having seen panels with good spread across institution types, which is desirable to capture different perspectives and avoid homogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match reviewer expertise to application content
rubrics_metrics.description: Select reviewers based on close content/expertise matching to the application (e.g., automated/content-based matching such as keyword/regular-expression analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR experiment described: a 'college of reviewers' where reviewers are matched to applications using feature/keyword extraction from abstracts and reviewers' publications, aiming for content-appropriate matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate favoritism toward well-ensconced applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and review processes should reduce bias where reviewers favor applicants who are well known within the panel's expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters note reviewers may give better scores to those 'ensconced' in the panel's network. Proposed mitigations include broader reviewer pools, additional reviewers, and content-matching micro-panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewer quality and manage variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and address wide variation in reviewer quality; aim to select reviewers who provide substantive, well-supported critiques rather than generic or lazy comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions include increasing the number of reviews per application, using super panels for borderline cases, and training/expectations enforced by SROs and chairs. Commenters report senior reviewers can be more generic, while juniors may be erratic but more method-knowledgeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple reviewers per application (e.g., 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase the number of independent reviews per application (CIHR plan: 5 reviews) to reduce individual reviewer bias and allow relative ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR's model expects each reviewer to review many applications and rank them; multiple independent rankings enable mass sorting and identify outliers for further scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider virtual review / college of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Move from in-person study sections to virtual review systems where a standing 'college' of reviewers is matched to applications remotely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR's planned shift aims to improve expertise matching and reduce assembly difficulties; tradeoffs include loss of in-person discussion, which may be important for deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust conflict-of-interest management
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle conflicts of interest carefully; geographic concentrations or a thin pool can cause panels to be distorted by conflicts and force many recusals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR example: a thinner pool (e.g., many applicants from Montreal/Toronto) can lead to mass departures of panelists due to conflicts, requiring careful management or broader pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance reviewer career-stage and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose panels with a balance of junior and senior reviewers: juniors bring up-to-date method knowledge and willingness to use full scoring range; seniors bring broader perspective and historical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments observe juniors often use full 9-point scoring and may be harsher on significance/investigator/environment due to less historical knowledge; seniors sometimes provide more generic reviews. Both strengths and weaknesses exist in each group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent and equitable Early Career Reviewer (ECR) selection
rubrics_metrics.description: ECR programs should have transparent selection criteria and equitable access, rather than favoring 'up-and-coming stars' from top institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters report ECR slots are limited (e.g., two per section), selection appears to favor white males from top R1s, and applicants have received dismissive rejections despite having independent research credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer familiarity with applicants' track records
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider that reviewers' knowledge of an applicant's past contributions affects scoring on investigator and environment criteria; panels should account for unequal background knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Junior reviewers may undervalue investigator track record and institutional environment because they haven't seen historic contributions or institutional strengths, causing scoring discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overemphasis on grantsmanship/grantsmithing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not let stylistic or superficial presentation issues (e.g., prose/formatting minutiae) disproportionately determine funding outcomes when the underlying idea is strong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion of 'grantsmithing' indicates panels sometimes reject grants for minor presentation issues. Recognize many very good proposals exist; focus should remain on scientific merit rather than commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on MDs solely for clinical relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting many MDs to satisfy 'translational' expertise can be problematic if they lack skill in evaluating hypothesis quality and basic-science approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenter notes proliferation of MDs on panels who understand clinical relevance but may not judge a good hypothesis; ensure content expertise aligns with review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and discourage boilerplate or lazy reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify reviewers who routinely provide boilerplate, unsupported, or disengaged comments and take steps to improve accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boilerplate reviews may arise from fatigue or low morale; chairs and SROs should enforce standards and foster meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ad hoc reviewers to supplement regular members
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in ad hoc reviewers each cycle to broaden expertise and improve diversity beyond the regular membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad hocs can improve topical coverage and demographic diversity but do not fully substitute for a well-composed regular panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic representation and national spread
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure panels represent a geographic spread, avoiding purely coastal or purely 'flyover' compositions and reflecting national applicant distribution appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes good geographic spreading in panels, sometimes overrepresenting 'flyoverlandia'; geographic balance is important but has tradeoffs with expertise matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms for removing problematic permanent appointees
rubrics_metrics.description: Have processes to rotate off or otherwise address persistent problematic reviewers (e.g., a 'nutjob' senior permanent appointee) who degrade panel functioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters cite relief when problematic long-term members rotate off; panels benefit from the ability to refresh membership and address chronic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rank-based sorting and super panels for borderline decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify applications with extreme reviewer disagreement (high z-scores) and route them to super panels or additional review for more considered cutoff decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR example: super panels would evaluate applications with biggest z-scores among reviewers to hone the funding cut-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce reviewer adherence to SRO/CSR instructions and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect reviewers, particularly senior ones, to follow SRO/CSR guidance (which may change yearly) and provide consistent application of review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments report some senior reviewers ignoring instructions; consistent enforcement and reviewer training can reduce variability and 'old-school vs newschool' differences.
